description: A field-neutral course on how to plan, run, report and defend research in any computing discipline: turning a topic into a question, reading the literature, designing reproducible experiments, handling statistical evidence, working ethically, and writing and presenting results. Students practise on ethics scenarios, computational notebooks and a research proposal they develop through the term.
modelledOn: Booth, Colomb and Williams, The Craft of Research
Wohlin, Runeson, Host, Ohlsson, Regnell and Wesslen, Experimentation in Software Engineering
Committee on Publication Ethics guidelines and the Singapore Statement on Research Integrity
outcomes: Formulate a focused, answerable and ethical research question with testable hypotheses in a chosen computing field.
Search, read and critically appraise the literature and synthesise it to justify a research gap.
Design a controlled, reproducible study and identify its threats to validity.
Analyse data with appropriate statistics, quantify uncertainty and report results honestly.
Identify ethical issues in a study, obtain the right approvals and protect participants and data.
Write a research proposal and a paper section, review a peer's work, and present and defend a project.

units.title: Research questions and design
topics: Kinds of research in computing: empirical, theoretical, design science and engineering
From topic to question: narrowing, feasibility and significance
Hypotheses, claims, falsifiability and kinds of contribution
Operationalising constructs: variables, metrics and measurement validity
Choosing a design: quantitative, qualitative and mixed methods
Scoping with real constraints: data access, compute, time and local context

units.title: Literature search and critical reading
topics: Search strategy: databases, keywords, Boolean queries and citation chasing
Narrative and systematic reviews; the PRISMA flow diagram
Reading a paper in three passes; appraisal checklists
Synthesis: concept matrices, themes and identifying a gap
Reference managers, citation styles and avoiding plagiarism
Judging sources: predatory venues, preprints and retractions

units.title: Experimental design and reproducibility
topics: Controlled experiments: baselines, controls and ablations
Sampling, randomisation, blocking and confounds
Threats to validity: internal, external, construct and conclusion
Reproducibility and replicability: seeds, environments and containers
Data and code management: version control, notebooks, documentation and FAIR data
Benchmarks, measurement error and simulation studies

units.title: Statistical evidence and reporting
topics: Descriptive statistics, distributions, outliers and honest graphics
Estimation, standard errors, confidence intervals and the bootstrap
Hypothesis tests, p-values, power and sample size
Effect sizes and multiple comparisons: family-wise error and false discovery rate
Non-parametric tests and comparing systems across datasets
Regression models and a Bayesian summary of evidence
Reporting pitfalls: p-hacking, selective reporting, and the garden of forking paths

units.title: Qualitative and mixed methods
topics: Surveys: questionnaire design, sampling frames and response bias
Interviews and focus groups, including with low-literacy participants
Thematic analysis, coding and inter-rater agreement
Case studies and evaluating a designed artefact
User studies and usability evaluation

units.title: Research ethics and integrity
topics: Core principles: respect for persons, beneficence and justice; informed consent
Ethics review boards and approval processes; working in Ghana and across Africa
Misconduct: fabrication, falsification, plagiarism and questionable practices
Conflicts of interest, authorship and credit; dual-use and responsible technology
Community engagement, benefit sharing and avoiding extractive research
Data protection, anonymisation and the secure handling of research data

units.title: Academic writing, proposals and peer review
topics: The structure of a paper: introduction, method, results and discussion
Abstracts, claims and related work
Figures, tables and clear reporting of results
The peer review process: writing a review and responding to reviewers
Publishing: venues, open access, preprints and author contributions
Writing a research proposal: aims, plan, timeline and budget

units.title: Presenting and defending research
topics: Structuring a talk and its slides
Posters and lightning talks
Handling questions and defending design choices
Planning a thesis: supervision, milestones and time management

schedule.title: Kinds of research and good questions
schedule.exercise: Take a broad topic from your field, write three candidate research questions, and rate each for feasibility, significance and testability with a short justification.

tasks.title: Classify 8 short project abstracts as empirical, theoretical, design science or engineering work, and justify each label with evidence from the text
Narrow a broad topic into a focused question across three rounds of feedback in a scenario, and score each version for scope and answerability
Rewrite 6 vague claims as testable hypotheses, name the observation that would refute each, and check which ones a given dataset can address

schedule.title: Measurement, design choices and scope
schedule.exercise: Operationalise the construct 'usable' or 'accurate' for your own question with a metric, an instrument and a validity argument, and choose a design with reasons.

tasks.title: Compute precision, recall and F1 for a classifier from given counts and state what each metric hides about the construct being measured
Pick a design for a research problem in a scenario, choosing among experiment, survey and case study, and score the fit with the question
Rescope a proposal after a scenario cuts its data access and compute budget, keeping the question answerable, and defend the revised plan

schedule.title: Searching and reading the literature
schedule.exercise: Write a search string with synonyms and Boolean operators for your question, record the number of hits at each screening stage, and summarise one paper after a three-pass reading.

tasks.title: Refine a search query over four rounds in a scenario, adding synonyms and exclusions, and score recall and precision of the results
Tabulate 120 screened records into a PRISMA flow count, remove duplicates by title matching in code, and report included and excluded numbers
Appraise a paper with a hidden flaw in its evaluation in a scenario, listing the evidence for each concern and rating the reliability of its claims

schedule.title: Synthesis, citation and source quality
schedule.exercise: Build a concept matrix for ten papers on your topic and write a paragraph that identifies the gap the matrix shows.

tasks.title: Spot the paraphrasing that counts as plagiarism among 6 passages in a scenario, and repair each with a correct citation
Load a table of 40 papers with their methods and datasets, build a concept matrix with a script, and find the combination no paper has tried
Judge 8 sources in a scenario, including a retracted paper and an unreviewed preprint, and decide which can support a claim in your review

schedule.title: Controlled experiments and sampling
schedule.exercise: Design an experiment comparing two methods in your field with a baseline, an ablation and a sampling plan, and list the three biggest threats to its validity.

tasks.title: Randomly assign 40 participants to two groups with blocking by experience level, and check that the groups are balanced on three covariates
Run a method with and without each of 3 components on a dataset, tabulate the ablation results, and report which components matter
Find the threats to internal, external and construct validity in a flawed study design in a scenario, and propose a fix for each

schedule.title: Reproducibility and research data management
schedule.exercise: Write the README and environment file that would let a stranger reproduce your main experiment, and list what could still differ between machines.

tasks.title: Run a notebook with a random element ten times, show that results differ, then fix the seed and record the environment versions
Organise a messy analysis into a clean project with data, code and results folders, a run script and a short data dictionary
Run a Monte Carlo simulation study of two estimators over 1000 repetitions, report bias and variance, and test sensitivity to the random seed

schedule.title: Describing data, estimation and tests
schedule.exercise: Compute a confidence interval and a bootstrap interval for a mean difference, run a test, and report the effect size and the sample size you would need for 80 percent power.

tasks.title: Summarise a skewed dataset with mean, median and spread, plot its histogram and box plot, and flag outliers with a stated rule
Compute a bootstrap confidence interval for a median difference between two groups with 5000 resamples and compare it with a t interval
Estimate by simulation the power of a two-group test at three effect sizes and four sample sizes, and choose the smallest adequate sample

schedule.title: Comparing systems and reporting honestly
schedule.exercise: Compare three methods across eight datasets with an appropriate test, then write the results paragraph in a way that reports uncertainty and every analysis that was tried.

tasks.title: Run a rank-based test on paired scores of two methods over 10 datasets and report the statistic, p-value and effect size
Fit a regression of runtime on input size and hardware type, check residuals, and report coefficients with intervals
Test 40 hypotheses on random noise data, count false positives with and without false discovery control, and show how selective reporting inflates results

schedule.title: Surveys, interviews and qualitative analysis
schedule.exercise: Write 8 neutral survey questions for your topic, plan the sampling, and code ten interview excerpts into themes with a second coder.

tasks.title: Fix 8 leading, double-barrelled or ambiguous questions in a draft survey in a scenario, and score the improvement in neutrality
Compute the kappa agreement statistic for two coders over 60 coded interview segments and decide whether agreement is good enough to proceed
Plan a usability study of a mobile-money screen in a scenario, choosing tasks, participants and measures, and score threats to the findings

schedule.title: Ethical principles, review boards and misconduct
schedule.exercise: Draft the informed consent text for a study in a Ghanaian community and list what an ethics board would ask you to change.

tasks.title: Review a consent form in a scenario, find 5 missing or unclear elements, and rewrite it in plain language for first-time participants
Prepare an ethics application for a school study in a scenario, deciding what risks, safeguards and approvals to describe, and score completeness
Investigate a suspected image duplication in a student's results in a scenario, weighing evidence, due process and the response, and score fairness

schedule.title: Authorship, community and data protection
schedule.exercise: Allocate authorship order for a six-person project from a contribution table and justify it with an agreed set of criteria.

tasks.title: Settle an authorship dispute in a scenario using contribution records and agreed criteria, and score the fairness of the outcome
Remove direct identifiers and generalise quasi-identifiers in a 500-row study table, then check how many participants remain unique
Plan engagement with a farming community whose data a research team wants to use in a scenario, covering consent, benefits and sharing of results

schedule.title: Writing papers, reviews and proposals
schedule.exercise: Write a one-page proposal with aims, method, timeline and budget, and write a half-page review of a peer's proposal listing strengths, weaknesses and questions.

tasks.title: Redraw a cluttered results plot with clear labels, units, uncertainty bars and a caption that states the finding in one sentence
Write a review of a draft paper in a scenario, scoring soundness, novelty and clarity, and respond to a hostile reviewer comment with evidence
Assemble a proposal with aims, work plan and a three-month budget in a scenario, and defend it to a funding panel that cuts the budget by a third

schedule.title: Presenting, defending and planning the thesis
schedule.exercise: Deliver a five-minute talk on your proposal, answer three hard questions from peers, and write a milestone plan for the next six months.

tasks.title: Reorder and cut 14 slides of a talk in a scenario to fit five minutes, keeping the question, method, result and take-away
Answer 6 hard questions from a mock panel in a scenario, including one you cannot answer, and score honesty, evidence and composure
Build a six-month thesis plan as a task table with dependencies and compute the critical path and the slack for each task
